questions.question: A merchant marks his products 30% above the cost price and provides a 10% discount on the marked price. What percent profit does he earn?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the successive percentage formula: **Net Profit %** = x + y + (xy ÷ 100)

Here, markup (x) = +30 and discount (y) = −10.

Net Profit % = 30 − 10 + [30 × (−10)] ÷ 100

Net Profit % = 20 − 3 = 17%

**∴ The correct answer is 17%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of the product be 100 units.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bd7a80747db5e2dd085af30eb5ccd549883c728be75f7cc5dfb53bc6ee19b86c.png] 

**Given:** **Markup %** = 30%, **Discount %** = 10%.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = CP + 30% of CP

⇒ **MP** = 100 + (30 ÷ 100 × 100) = 130 units.

⇒ **Discount** = 10% of MP = 10 ÷ 100 × 130 = 13 units.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = MP − Discount

⇒ **SP** = 130 − 13 = 117 units.

⇒ **Profit** = SP − CP = 117 − 100 = 17 units.

⇒ **Profit %** = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (17 ÷ 100) × 100 = 17%.

**∴ The correct answer is 17%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between MP and CP

The ratio of **Marked Price** to **Cost Price** is given by: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂% are given, the equivalent single discount is (d₁ + d₂ − d₁d₂ ÷ 100)%.

Selling Price Formula

**Selling Price** can be calculated directly from the **Marked Price** as SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 12 days and 24 days, respectively. Both work for 2 days and then A leaves. How long (in days) will B take to complete the remaining work?

Work done by **(A + B)** in **2 days** = (2 + 1) × 2 = **6 units**. **Remaining work** = 24 − 6 = **18 units**. Time taken by **B** alone = 18 ÷ 1 = **18 days**. **∴ The correct answer is 18 days.**

questions.question: If the fourth proportional to 5, 15, and 25 is k, then find k.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If **a, b, c, d** are in **proportion**, then **a × d = b × c**.

Given: 5, 15, 25, k are in proportion.

5 × k = 15 × 25

k = 3 × 25 = 75 (Since 15 ÷ 5 = 3)

**∴ The correct answer is k = 75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First term (a) = 5

Second term (b) = 15

Third term (c) = 25

**Fourth proportional** = k

**Formula Used:**

For four numbers to be in proportion: a ÷ b = c ÷ d

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e42ad68061711222b74a0326f762631e473a4d56c4b19d20f36628172f13db0a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 5 ÷ 15 = 25 ÷ k

⇒ 1 ÷ 3 = 25 ÷ k

⇒ k = 25 × 3

⇒ k = 75

**∴ The correct answer is k = 75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers **a** and **b** is √(a × b).

Third Proportional

If **a, b, c** are in continued proportion, then **a : b = b : c**, and **c = b² ÷ a** is the third proportional.

Product Property

In any proportion, the **product of extremes** (outer terms) is always equal to the **product of means** (inner terms).

questions.question: The price of an article is first increased by 30% and then decreased by 20%. Due to these successive changes, the final price becomes ₹40 more than the original price. What is the original price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage change = a + b + (ab/100)

Here, a = +30 and b = −20

Net change = 30 − 20 + (30 × (−20) / 100) = 10 − 6 = 4%

Since 4% change corresponds to ₹40 increase, then 100% (original price) = (40 ÷ 4) × 100 = ₹1,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First **increase** = 30%

Second **decrease** = 20%

Difference between **final price** and **original price** = ₹40

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51b05953eb9c9b901707771e0672a2c4568d2eb545daed44bd19ded8c47820d2.png] 

Let the **original price** of the article be ₹ x.

⇒ Price after 30% increase = x + (30 ÷ 100) × x = 1.3x

⇒ Price after 20% decrease = 1.3x − (20 ÷ 100) × 1.3x

⇒ Final Price = 1.3x − 0.26x = 1.04x

⇒ Given: Final Price − Original Price = ₹40

⇒ 1.04x − x = 40

⇒ 0.04x = 40

⇒ x = 40 ÷ 0.04

⇒ x = 4000 ÷ 4 = 1000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is changed by a% and then by b%, the effective change is given by [a + b + (ab/100)]%.

Multiplying Factor Method

An increase of x% is equivalent to multiplying the value by (1 + x/100), and a decrease of y% is equivalent to multiplying by (1 − y/100).

Ratio Method for Successive Changes

Convert percentages to fractions (30% = 13/10 and −20% = 4/5). Multiply the ratios: (13/10) × (4/5) = 52/50 = 104/100, which shows a 4% increase.

questions.question: Two articles are sold at the same selling price. On one article, the trader makes a 25% profit, and on the other, he incurs a 25% loss. What is the overall percentage loss?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two articles are sold at the same **Selling Price**, one at a **gain of x%** and the other at a **loss of x%**, the transaction always results in an **overall loss**.

Net Loss % = (x / 10)²

Given x = 25%

Net Loss % = (25 / 10)² = (2.5)² = 6.25%

**∴ The correct answer is 6.25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Selling Price (SP)** is same for both articles. 1st article profit = **25%**, 2ⁿd article loss = **25%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7e21bb2a5952a2f14305448bed6a56542a068b6feb348f7dca45c26c036ad334.png] 

⇒ For 1st article (25% profit): 25% = 1/4 → **CP₁** : **SP₁** = 4 : 5

⇒ For 2ⁿd article (25% loss): 25% = 1/4 → **CP₂** : **SP₂** = 4 : 3

⇒ To make **Selling Prices** equal, take LCM(5, 3) = 15 units.

⇒ Article 1: **CP₁** = 4 × 3 = 12 units | **SP₁** = 5 × 3 = 15 units

⇒ Article 2: **CP₂** = 4 × 5 = 20 units | **SP₂** = 3 × 5 = 15 units

⇒ **Total Cost Price** = 12 + 20 = 32 units

⇒ **Total Selling Price** = 15 + 15 = 30 units

⇒ **Overall Loss %** = [(32 − 30) / 32] × 100 = (2 / 32) × 100 = 6.25%

**∴ The correct answer is 6.25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Percentage Change Rule

For two successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the net change is given by (a + b + ab/100)%. However, when SP is same, the shortcut (x/10)² is derived from specific CP adjustments.

Same Cost Price Case

If two articles are bought at the same **Cost Price (CP)** and sold at x% profit and x% loss respectively, there is **No Profit No Loss** overall.

Profit and Loss Ratios

Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100 and Loss % = (Loss / CP) × 100. Always ensure the denominator is **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise.

questions.question: Three positive integers a, b, and c satisfy the following conditions: (i) a and b are coprime, (ii) b and c are coprime, (iii) a and c are not coprime, (iv) abc = 360. The minimum possible value of a + b + c is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Prime factorization of **360** = 2³ × 3² × 5 = 8 × 9 × 5.

To minimize the sum, **a**, **b**, and **c** should be as close to √³(360) ≈ 7.1 as possible.

Condition (iii) requires **a** and **c** to share a factor, so we split the 2³ into 2² for **a** and 2¹ for **c**.

Assigning factors: **a** = 2² = 4, **b** = 3² = 9, **c** = 2 × 5 = 10.

Check: gcd(4, 9)=1, gcd(9, 10)=1, gcd(4, 10)=2. All conditions satisfied.

Minimum sum = 4 + 9 + 10 = 23.

**∴ The correct answer is 23.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** abc = 360, gcd(a, b) = 1, gcd(b, c) = 1, gcd(a, c) > 1.

**Prime Factorization:** 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5¹.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9ab8045a186c09eeb61e6c94b5207c8920af8623e59d78a36a7cfe65ce1153c8.png] 

⇒ Total **prime factors** available are {2, 2, 2}, {3, 3}, {5}.

⇒ For **gcd(a, c) > 1**, both **a** and **c** must share at least one prime factor (2, 3, or 5).

⇒ If we share prime 2: **a** contains 2x and **c** contains 2y. Since **b** is coprime to both, **b** cannot have any factor of 2.

⇒ Trial 1: **b** = 3² = 9. Then **ac** = 360 ÷ 9 = 40. Since **a, c** are even, possible pairs (a, c) are (4, 10), (2, 20). Sums: 4+9+10 = **23**; 2+9+20 = 31.

⇒ Trial 2: **b** = 5. Then **ac** = 360 ÷ 5 = 72. To share a factor and keep sum low, try (a, c) = (6, 12). Sum: 6+5+12 = **23**.

⇒ Trial 3: **b** = 8. Then **ac** = 360 ÷ 8 = 45. To share a factor, try (a, c) = (3, 15). Sum: 3+8+15 = 26.

⇒ Comparing all valid combinations, the minimum sum is 23.

**∴ The correct answer is 23.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Coprime Numbers

Two numbers are **coprime** if their **Greatest Common Divisor (GCD)** is 1. They do not share any prime factors.

Prime Factorization

Every composite number can be expressed as a unique product of **prime powers**. For 360, it is 2³ × 3² × 5¹.

AM-GM Inequality Concept

For a fixed product, the sum of positive numbers is **minimized** when the numbers are as close to each other as possible (ideally equal to the n-th root).

questions.question: Find the third proportional to 240 and 120.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of the first two numbers is **240 : 120 = 2 : 1**.

For the **third proportional** (c), the ratio **120 : c** must also be **2 : 1**.

Since the ratio is halved, **c = 120 ÷ 2 = 60**.

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First term (a) = **240**

Second term (b) = **120**

**Formula Used:**

If three numbers **a, b, and c** are in **continued proportion**, then:

a : b :: b : c ⇒ c = b² ÷ a

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bd5ddac681c888fb87a5d5a28513b9f5887279f30ea9072b6210e1f4b674bb2f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **third proportional** be c.

⇒ 240 : 120 = 120 : c

⇒ 240 ÷ 120 = 120 ÷ c

⇒ 2 = 120 ÷ c

⇒ c = 120 ÷ 2

⇒ c = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The **Mean Proportional** between two numbers x and y is given by the formula √(x × y).

Fourth Proportional

If four numbers a, b, c, and d are in proportion (a : b = c : d), then **d** is the **Fourth Proportional**, calculated as (b × c) ÷ a.

Product Rule

In any proportion, the **Product of Extremes** (first and last terms) is always equal to the **Product of Means** (middle terms).

questions.question: A certain sum amounts to ₹5,200 in 2 years and ₹6,400 in 4 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ **Simple Interest (SI)** for 2 years = ₹6,400 − ₹5,200 = ₹1,200 **Principal (P)** = Amount after 2 years − SI for 2 years = ₹5,200 − ₹1,200 = ₹4,000 **Rate (R)** = (SI for 2 years × 100) ÷ (P × Time) Rate = (1,200 × 100) ÷ (4,000 × 2) = 15% **∴ The correct answer is 15 percent.**

questions.question: The average of 8 numbers is 45. If each number is decreased by 3, what will the new average be?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If each number in a set is **decreased** by a constant value **k**, the **average** of the set also **decreases** by the same value **k**.

Given **Old Average** = 45 and **Decrease** per number = 3.

**New Average** = 45 − 3 = 42.

**∴ The correct answer is 42.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Total numbers** = 8

**Initial Average** = 45

**Formula Used:**

Average = **Sum of observations** ÷ **Number of observations**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/315eab75c4548ca46480e86e5dc43f64b907a9a30d80d17f10abbad032df887b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Initial Sum** = Average × Count = 45 × 8 = 360

⇒ **Total Reduction** = 8 × 3 = 24

⇒ **New Sum** = 360 − 24 = 336

⇒ **New Average** = 336 ÷ 8

⇒ **New Average** = 42

**∴ The correct answer is 42.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Addition Rule

If **k** is added to every observation, the new average is **Old Average + k**.

Multiplication Rule

If every observation is multiplied by a constant **n**, the new average becomes **Old Average × n**.

Division Rule

If every observation is divided by a non-zero constant **m**, the new average is **Old Average ÷ m**.

questions.question: If 45% of a number exceeds 20% of it by 30, then the number is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Percentage difference** = 45% − 20% = 25%

The question states that this 25% **difference** is equal to 30.

Using the **Unitary method**:

25% → 30

100% → 30 × (100 ÷ 25) = 30 × 4 = 120

**∴ The correct answer is 120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 45% of a **number** exceeds 20% of the same **number** by 30.

**Formula Used:** Percentage of a number = (Percent ÷ 100) × Number

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fea777d81e8ac98a15d6fc95dc6cf67f71a2b127b1ad767a5058b535995da93f.png] 
⇒ Let the **number** be x. ⇒ (45% of x) − (20% of x) = 30 ⇒ (45/100) × x − (20/100) × x = 30 ⇒ (45 − 20)/100 × x = 30 ⇒ (25/100) × x = 30 ⇒ (1/4) × x = 30 ⇒ x = 30 × 4 ⇒ x = 120

**∴ The correct answer is 120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To solve quickly, remember common fractions: 25% = 1/4, 20% = 1/5, 50% = 1/2, and 75% = 3/4.

Base Value Property

When comparing two percentages of the same **number**, you can directly subtract or add the percentage values before applying them to the **base**.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage change = (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100. This is used to find how much one value is greater or smaller than another in percentage terms.

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 54. If three times the smaller number exceeds twice the larger number by 6, find the difference between the two numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **smaller number** be x. Then the **larger number** is 54 − x.

Given condition: 3 × x − 2 × (54 − x) = 6

⇒ 3x − 108 + 2x = 6 ⇒ 5x = 114 ⇒ x = 22.8.

**Larger number** = 54 − 22.8 = 31.2.

**Difference** = 31.2 − 22.8 = 8.4.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of two numbers = 54. Let **smaller number** = x and **larger number** = y.

**Formulas:** (i) x + y = 54 | (ii) 3x − 2y = 6

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a7b5faf940cb5be7279675416fbc44185980b9ddc416778f222aceaa37eee19b.png] 

⇒ From (i), y = 54 − x.

⇒ Substitute y in (ii): 3x − 2(54 − x) = 6

⇒ 3x − 108 + 2x = 6

⇒ 5x = 114 ⇒ x = 22.8

⇒ y = 54 − 22.8 = 31.2

⇒ **Difference** = y − x = 31.2 − 22.8 = 8.4

**∴ The correct answer is 8.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

Equations of the form ax + by = c can be solved using the **Elimination Method** or **Substitution Method** to find unique values for the variables.

Sum and Difference Relation

If the **Sum (S)** and **Difference (D)** of two numbers are known, the Larger number = (S + D) ÷ 2 and the Smaller number = (S − D) ÷ 2.

Algebraic Modeling

Key phrases like **exceeds** or **more than** indicate subtraction (Larger − Smaller = Difference) when setting up equations.

questions.question: A ladder of length 8 m is placed against a vertical wall, making an angle of 60° with the ground. How high does the ladder reach up the wall?

questions.question: In a triangle, the ratio of three angles is 3 : 3 : 4. Find the measure of the largest angle.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total units in the **ratio** = 3 + 3 + 4 = 10 units.

Sum of **angles** in a **triangle** = 180°.

10 units → 180°

1 unit → 18°

Measure of the **largest angle** (4 units) = 4 × 18° = 72°.

**∴ The correct answer is 72degree.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of three **angles** = 3 : 3 : 4

**Formula Used:**

The **Angle-Sum Property** of a **triangle** states that the sum of all **interior angles** is exactly 180°.

questions.question:
The sides of a rectangular field are 77 m and 98 m long. Its area is equal to the area of a circular field. What is the perimeter (in m) of the circular field?

(Take pi = (22)/(7) )
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of Rectangle = Area of Circle ⇒ 98 × 77 = (22/7) × r²

r² = (98 × 77 × 7) ÷ 22 ⇒ r² = 49 × 11 × 7 × 7 ÷ 11 × 2 ÷ 2 (Simplifying: 98 = 49 × 2 and 77 = 11 × 7)

r² = 49 × 49 ⇒ **r = 49 m**

Perimeter of Circle = 2 × (22/7) × 49 = 44 × 7 = **308 m**

**∴ The correct answer is 308 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Length of rectangular field = 98 m, Breadth = 77 m. Area of circle = Area of rectangle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ba00c9f7064fd69d8a241444bb8987183b379382bad60db2fe7600caef8b98f8.png] 

⇒ Area of **Rectangular Field** = Length × Breadth

⇒ Area = 98 × 77 = **7546 m²**

⇒ Area of **Circular Field** = πr²

⇒ Since Area of Circle = Area of Rectangle:

⇒ (22/7) × r² = 7546

⇒ r² = (7546 × 7) ÷ 22

⇒ r² = 343 × 7 = **2401**

⇒ Radius (r) = √2401 = **49 m**

⇒ **Perimeter (Circumference)** of Circular Field = 2 × π × r

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × (22/7) × 49 = 2 × 22 × 7 = **308 m**

**∴ The correct answer is 308 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area and Perimeter of a Rectangle

The **Area** is length × breadth (l × b) and the **Perimeter** is 2(l + b).

Circle Mensuration Formulas

For a circle of **radius** r, the Area = πr² and the **Circumference** (Perimeter) = 2πr.

Relation Between Radius and Area

If the radius is multiplied by a factor k, the **Area** increases by k² and the **Perimeter** increases by k.

questions.question: A team of 3 workers, P, Q, and R, is assigned to paint a large wall. P alone can finish the work in 14 days, Q alone in 21 days, and R alone in 42 days. If they start together but P leaves after 4 days, and the remaining work is completed by Q and R together, in how many total days is the wall completely painted?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Total Work** = LCM(14, 21, 42) = 42 units.

Efficiencies: **P** = 3, **Q** = 2, **R** = 1. Combined (P+Q+R) = 6.

Work done in **4 days** = 6 × 4 = 24 units.

Remaining work = 42 − 24 = 18 units.

Time for **Q and R** to finish = 18 ÷ (2 + 1) = 6 days.

**Total time** = 4 + 6 = 10 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ All three started together, so combined efficiency = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 units/day.

⇒ Work completed by **P, Q, and R** in **4 days** = 6 × 4 = 24 units.

⇒ Remaining work to be done = 42 − 24 = 18 units.

⇒ Since **P** left, **Q and R** complete the remaining work.

Efficiency and Time

questions.question: The average of 6.5, 10.8, 20 and a is 13. The value of a is:

Assume the **mean** 13 as the balance point for all deviations.

Net deviation from 13: (6.5 − 13) + (10.8 − 13) + (20 − 13) + (a − 13) = 0

⇒ −6.5 − 2.2 + 7.0 + (a − 13) = 0

⇒ −1.7 + (a − 13) = 0

⇒ a − 13 = 1.7 ⇒ a = 13 + 1.7 = 14.7

**∴ The correct answer is 14.7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers = 6.5, 10.8, 20, a | **Total Count** (n) = 4 | **Average** = 13

**Formula Used:** Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/55b816b14c77cb4776eb8fd207f6c608d886e705bb5763a4aab9f35c6088d70e.png] 

⇒ Sum of observations = Average × Count

⇒ 6.5 + 10.8 + 20 + a = 13 × 4

⇒ 37.3 + a = 52

⇒ a = 52 − 37.3

⇒ a = 14.7

**∴ The correct answer is 14.7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean Properties

If each observation is increased or decreased by a constant **k**, the **new average** also increases or decreases by **k**.

Sum of Deviations

The sum of **deviations** of all observations from their **mean** is always **zero** (Σ(xᵢ − x̄) = 0).

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the **combined average** = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

questions.question: Four identical cubes are placed one after another and the length of the cuboid so formed is 256 cm. Find the volume of a single cube.

questions.question: Two trains are moving in opposite directions at speeds of 8 m/s and 10 m/s. If they completely pass each other in 8 seconds, find the combined length of both trains.

⇒ When two objects move in **opposite directions**, Relative Speed (SR) = v₁ + v₂

questions.question: The sum of the ages of two siblings is 28 years and the difference of their ages is 8 years. What is the present age of the elder sibling?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **larger value** (Elder Sibling) when the **Sum** and **Difference** are given:

**Elder Sibling Age** = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2

⇒ Age = (28 + 8) ÷ 2

⇒ Age = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 years

**∴ The correct answer is 18 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of ages = 28 years

Difference of ages = 8 years

**Method:** Linear Equations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ae7169f8da72d3b4c53ec5ab7235ecf23031eafe55aac5cb8b42185ee4e3b683.png] 

⇒ Let the age of the **elder sibling** be x years and the **younger sibling** be y years.

⇒ x + y = 28 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ x − y = 8 --- (Equation 2)

⇒ Adding Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ (x + y) + (x − y) = 28 + 8

⇒ 2x = 36

⇒ x = 36 ÷ 2

⇒ x = 18 years

**∴ The correct answer is 18 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum and Difference Formula

For any two numbers x and y, if Sum = S and Difference = D, then the larger number x = (S + D) ÷ 2 and the smaller number y = (S − D) ÷ 2.

Age Ratio Problems

If the ratio of ages of two people is a : b, their ages can be taken as ax and bx. The difference between their ages remains **constant** throughout their lives.

Average Age

The average age of n persons is the sum of their ages divided by n. If each person's age increases by 'k' years, the average also increases by 'k' years.

questions.question: At what annual interest rate will a principal amount of ₹1,000 become ₹1,728 in a period of 1 year and 6 months, assuming that the interest is compounded semi-annually?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Amount** to **Principal** = 1728 : 1000.

Since interest is **compounded semi-annually** for 1.5 years, there are 3 half-yearly periods.

Take the cube root for one period: √³1728 : √³1000 = 12 : 10.

Rate per half-year = (12 − 10)/10 × 100 = 20%.

**Annual Interest Rate** = 20% × 2 = 40%.

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Principal (P)** = ₹1,000, **Amount (A)** = ₹1,728, **Time** = 1 year 6 months.

**Formula Used:** A = P(1 + r/200)²ⁿ (for semi-annual compounding, where r is annual rate and n is years).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2728be4f6f65d0e67e3a83f3129caf64906bdf76e0b06a749d1e7941956868ef.png] 

⇒ Total periods (n) = 1.5 years × 2 = 3 half-years.

⇒ 1728 = 1000 × (1 + r/200)³

⇒ 1728/1000 = (1 + r/200)³

⇒ 1.728 = (1 + r/200)³

⇒ √³(1.728) = 1 + r/200

⇒ 1.2 = 1 + r/200

⇒ r/200 = 1.2 − 1 = 0.2

⇒ r = 0.2 × 200 = 40%.

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Compounding Frequency

For semi-annual compounding, the rate is halved (r/2) and the time periods are doubled (2n). For quarterly, the rate is divided by 4 and periods multiplied by 4.

Effective Interest Rate

The actual interest earned over a year when compounding occurs more than once. Formula: E = (1 + r/k)k − 1, where k is compounding frequency per year.

Rule of 72

A quick way to estimate the time required to double an investment: Years to double ≈ 72 ÷ Annual Interest Rate.

questions.question: A shopkeeper fixes the marked price of an item 150% above its cost price. What percentage of discount on marked price should be allowed to gain 110%?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 100.

**Marked Price (MP)** is 150% above CP ⇒ 100 + 150 = 250.

To gain 110%, **Selling Price (SP)** must be 100 + 110 = 210.

**Discount** = MP − SP = 250 − 210 = 40.

**Discount %** = (40 ÷ 250) × 100 = 16%.

**∴ The correct answer is 16%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup = 150% above **Cost Price**

Required Profit = 110%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9dfdf3cf8c06ee8e809ae28cd294b654de1d41d375b2e27ce491fc7e0ae00b63.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Assume **CP** = 100 units

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + (150% of 100) = 100 + 150 = 250 units

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + (110% of 100) = 100 + 110 = 210 units

⇒ **Discount Amount** = MP − SP = 250 − 210 = 40 units

⇒ **Discount %** = (Discount Amount ÷ MP) × 100

⇒ **Discount %** = (40 ÷ 250) × 100

⇒ **Discount %** = 4 ÷ 25 × 100 = 16%

**∴ The correct answer is 16%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between CP, MP, Profit, and Discount

The ratio of MP to CP can be expressed as: MP/CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

Markup Percentage

Markup % is the percentage by which the cost price is increased to set the marked price: ((MP − CP) ÷ CP) × 100.

Effective Discount

For two successive discounts d₁ and d₂, the single equivalent discount is (d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: The sum of two positive numbers is 40 and their product is 175. The positive difference between them is:

Identify **factors** of the product **175** that add up to the sum **40**.

Factors of 175: 1 × 175, 5 × 35, 7 × 25.

Check **sum**: 5 + 35 = 40 (Correct).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Sum (x + y)** = 40 and **Product (xy)** = 175.

Formula: (x − y)² = (x + y)² − 4xy

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ce48dfd31a9836be2908d43943a0e14ca5d5c5ab407c3130c41935902865c388.png] 

⇒ (x − y)² = 40² − 4 × 175

⇒ (x − y)² = 1600 − 700

⇒ (x − y)² = 900

⇒ x − y = √900 = 30

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity

The relationship between sum, product, and difference is given by the identity: (a+b)² − (a−b)² = 4ab.

Quadratic Equations

If the sum (S) and product (P) are known, the numbers are roots of the equation: t² − St + P = 0.

Difference of Roots

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the positive difference of roots is given by √D / |a|, where D = b² − 4ac.

questions.question: If 3^x - 3x⁻¹ = 18 , then the value of (2x-1)/(2x+3) is:

Which of the following pairs of numbers is co-prime?

A) (15, 25)

B) (14, 35)

C) (9, 28)

D) (21, 49)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To identify **co-prime** numbers, check if the two numbers have any **common factor** other than 1.

(15, 25) → Both are divisible by 5.

(14, 35) → Both are divisible by 7.

(21, 49) → Both are divisible by 7.

(9, 28) → 9 = 3×3 and 28 = 2×2×7. No common prime factor exists.

**∴ The correct answer is (9, 28).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Pairs of numbers (15, 25), (14, 35), (9, 28), and (21, 49).

**Formula Used:** Two numbers are **co-prime** if their **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** is 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3b729b66551c51cfa9637f54cb8e53900b471cdafbfb774d686ae05741abc2f5.png] 

⇒ Factors of 15: 1, 3, 5, 15 | Factors of 25: 1, 5, 25. **HCF = 5**.

⇒ Factors of 14: 1, 2, 7, 14 | Factors of 35: 1, 5, 7, 35. **HCF = 7**.

⇒ Factors of 21: 1, 3, 7, 21 | Factors of 49: 1, 7, 49. **HCF = 7**.

⇒ Factors of 9: 1, 3, 9 | Factors of 28: 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28. **HCF = 1**.

**∴ The correct answer is (9, 28).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Definition of Co-prime Numbers

A set of numbers is co-prime if they have no common positive factor other than 1. Their **HCF** is always 1.

Consecutive Numbers

Any two **consecutive natural numbers** (e.g., 14 and 15, or 20 and 21) are always co-prime to each other.

LCM of Co-prime Numbers

The **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of two co-prime numbers is always equal to their **product** (a × b).

Prime Numbers Property

Any two **prime numbers** are always co-prime to each other since their only common factor is 1.

questions.question: A car travels from Gwalior to Jhansi at 60 km/hr and returns at 80 km/hr. If the total travel time is 3.5 hours, what is the one-way distance?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Direct Distance Formula** for **Total Travel Time**: **Distance = (S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂) × Total Time**.

Here, **S₁ = 60 km/hr**, **S₂ = 80 km/hr**, and **Total Time = 3.5 hr**.

⇒ Distance = (60 × 80) ÷ (60 + 80) × 3.5

⇒ Distance = (4800 ÷ 140) × 3.5 = (480 ÷ 14) × 3.5

⇒ Distance = 480 ÷ 4 = 120 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Speed from **Gwalior** to **Jhansi** = 60 km/hr, speed from **Jhansi** to **Gwalior** = 80 km/hr, and **Total travel time** = 3.5 hr.

**Formula Used:** Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f388e9c48b90381b46984cd35bc429d5d1a701d114a1a3c40a44c4723573d668.png] 

Let the **one-way distance** be **x** km.

⇒ Time taken to travel from Gwalior to Jhansi = x ÷ 60

⇒ Time taken to travel from Jhansi to Gwalior = x ÷ 80

⇒ Total Time = (x ÷ 60) + (x ÷ 80) = 3.5

⇒ (4x + 3x) ÷ 240 = 3.5

⇒ 7x ÷ 240 = 3.5

⇒ 7x = 3.5 × 240

⇒ 7x = 840

⇒ x = 840 ÷ 7 = 120 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed Formula

When a person travels the same distance at two different speeds S₁ and S₂, the **Average Speed** is given by (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Speed and Time Relation

For a constant distance, **Speed** is inversely proportional to **Time** (S₁ ÷ S₂ = T₂ ÷ T₁).

Distance when Time Difference is Given

If the difference in time (ΔT) is given instead of total time, the formula becomes: **Distance = (S₁ × S₂) ÷ |S₁ − S₂| × ΔT**.

questions.question: Joint Sitting of both the houses of the Parliament is summoned by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 108** of the **Constitution of India**, the **President** has the constitutional authority to summon a **Joint Sitting** of both the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• The **Joint Sitting** is a mechanism provided to resolve a **deadlock** between the two **Houses of Parliament** over the passage of a bill.
 
• A deadlock is deemed to have occurred if a bill passed by one House is rejected by the other, if the Houses disagree on **amendments**, or if more than **six months** elapse without the bill being passed by the second House.
 
• The **President** issues a notification or message expressing the intention to summon the members of both Houses to meet in a joint session for the purpose of deliberating and voting on the bill.
 
• Once the **President** notifies the intention to summon a joint sitting, neither House can proceed further with the bill independently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Presiding Officers:**

 
 
• While the **President** summons the session, the **Speaker of the Lok Sabha** presides over the joint sitting.
 
• In the absence of the Speaker, the **Deputy Speaker** of the Lok Sabha presides. If they are also absent, the **Deputy Chairman** of the **Rajya Sabha** takes the chair.
 
• The **Chairman of the Rajya Sabha** (the **Vice-President** of India) never presides over a joint sitting because they are not a member of either House of Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Applicability and Exceptions:**
 
 
• A joint sitting can only be convened for **Ordinary Bills** or **Financial Bills**.
 
• It cannot be summoned for a **Money Bill** (as the Lok Sabha has overriding powers) or a **Constitution Amendment Bill** (which must be passed by each House separately under **Article 368**).

questions.question: Which of the following physiographic regions of India is primarily formed by the extensive deposition of alluvium brought by the Himalayan river systems?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Northern Plains**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Northern Plains** of India were formed by the interplay of three major river systems: the **Indus**, the **Ganga**, and the **Brahmaputra**, along with their numerous tributaries.
 
• These rivers originate in the **Himalayas** and carry vast amounts of **silt** and **sedimentary debris** as they flow downstream toward the lower elevations.
 
• Over millions of years, these sediments were deposited in a vast basin located at the foothills of the **Himalayas**, creating a flat landmass composed entirely of **alluvial soil**.
 
• The plain spreads over an area of approximately **7 lakh sq. km**, stretching about **2400 km** in length and ranging between **240 to 320 km** in width.
 
• Due to the rich **alluvial deposits** and abundant water supply from the **perennial Himalayan rivers**, this region is one of the most **fertile** and **densely populated** physiographic divisions in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Peninsular Plateau**

 
 
• This is the **oldest landmass** of India, formed by the breaking and drifting of the **Gondwana land**.
 
• It consists of **igneous** and **metamorphic rocks** with gently rising hills and wide valleys, rather than deep alluvial deposits.
 
 
 
• **The Meghalaya Plateau**
 
 
• Geologically, it is an extension of the **Peninsular Plateau**, separated by the **Malda fault**.
 
• It is characterized by ancient crystalline rocks and receives the **highest rainfall** in the world at **Mawsynram**.
 
 
 
• **The Western Coastal Plains**
 
 
• These are narrow strips located between the **Western Ghats** and the **Arabian Sea**.
 
• Unlike the Northern Plains, they are formed by a combination of **submergence**, **emergence**, and the action of shorter **Peninsular rivers**.
 
 
 
• **Regional Divisions of Northern Plains**
 
 
• **Bhabar**: A narrow belt of pebbles at the foot of the **Shiwaliks**.
 
• **Terai**: A marshy, damp, and thickly forested region south of Bhabar.
 
• **Bhangar**: The older, less fertile alluvium containing **kankar** (calcareous deposits).
 
• **Kadar**: The newer, highly fertile **floodplain alluvium** renewed every year.

questions.question: Which practice supports sustainable agriculture by maintaining soil health?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Crop rotation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Crop rotation** is a core practice in **sustainable agriculture** that involves growing different types of crops in a planned sequence on the same land over successive seasons.
 
• It significantly enhances **soil fertility** by alternating crops with different nutrient needs; for instance, **leguminous plants** (like beans or pulses) are included to facilitate **biological nitrogen fixation**.
 
• Through **symbiotic relationships** with **Rhizobium bacteria** found in root nodules, these legumes convert atmospheric nitrogen into nitrates, naturally replenishing the soil for subsequent nitrogen-demanding crops like **maize** or **wheat**.
 
• The practice improves **soil structure** and **organic matter** levels by rotating deep-rooted and shallow-rooted plants, which aids in better **water infiltration** and prevents **soil compaction**.
 
• It serves as a natural **pest management** strategy by breaking the life cycles of **host-specific pathogens** and insects that thrive when a single crop is grown continuously.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monoculture farming**:

 
 
• Involves the repeated cultivation of only one crop species, leading to severe **nutrient depletion** and increased vulnerability to epidemics.
 
• Reduces **agrobiodiversity** and requires higher doses of synthetic chemicals to maintain yields.
 
 
 
• **Excessive chemical fertilisers**:
 
 
• While providing immediate nutrients, long-term use leads to **soil acidification** and the destruction of beneficial **microorganisms** like earthworms.
 
• Contributes to environmental issues such as **eutrophication** in nearby water bodies due to nutrient runoff.
 
 
 
• **Deforestation**:
 
 
• The clearing of forest land for agriculture results in massive **soil erosion** and the loss of the nutrient-rich **humus** layer.
 
• Disrupts the **carbon cycle** and leads to **habitat fragmentation**, which is the antithesis of sustainable land management.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is 3

questions.question: The Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 2025, enforced from 10 September 2025, is primarily intended to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Define carrier liability**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 2025** was introduced to modernize and replace the nearly century-old **Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 1925**, aligning Indian maritime law with contemporary international standards.
 
• The primary objective of this legislation is to provide a comprehensive legal framework that defines the **rights, responsibilities, liabilities, and immunities** of carriers (ship owners or charterers) and shippers (cargo owners) involved in the maritime transport of goods.
 
• It establishes the **statutory limits of liability** for loss or damage to cargo, ensuring that carriers cannot contract out of their basic obligations to provide a **seaworthy vessel** and properly handle goods.
 
• The Act incorporates principles from the **Hague-Visby Rules**, which determine the maximum compensation a carrier must pay per package or unit of weight in the event of cargo damage, thereby providing **legal certainty** to the global shipping industry.
 
• By clarifying the **burden of proof** and the specific instances where a carrier is exempt from liability (such as **Act of God** or **perils of the sea**), the law facilitates smoother dispute resolution in **Admiralty Courts**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• While the Carriage of Goods by Sea Act focuses on cargo liability, other maritime functions are regulated by distinct legislative frameworks:
 
 
• **Marine Pollution Control:** These matters are primarily governed by the **Merchant Shipping Act, 1958** and international conventions such as **MARPOL (International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships)**, which regulate the discharge of oil, sewage, and garbage into the ocean.
 
• **Port Infrastructure:** The development and administration of major ports in India fall under the **Major Port Authorities Act, 2021**, and schemes like the **Sagarmala Programme**, which focuses on port-led industrialization and connectivity.
 
• **Vessel Registration:** The technical requirements for the registration of ships, **tonnage measurement**, and the **nationality of vessels** are codified under the **Merchant Shipping Act** to ensure compliance with safety and security standards.
 
• **Bill of Lading:** The 2025 Act specifically addresses the **Bill of Lading** as a document of title, defining it as the primary evidence of the **contract of carriage** and receipt of goods.

questions.question: According to World Population Prospects, 2024, what is the estimated peak of the world’s population in the mid-2080s?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10.3 billion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Population Prospects 2024**, released by the **United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA)**, provides the latest official population estimates and projections, serving as a critical global demographic benchmark.
 
• According to the 2024 revision, the global population is projected to reach its peak at approximately **10.3 billion** people during the **mid-2080s**, specifically around the year **2084**.
 
• Following this peak, the report anticipates a gradual decline in the total number of people on Earth, with the population expected to settle at approximately **10.2 billion** by the year **2100**.
 
• This updated projection indicates that the global population peak will occur **earlier** and at a **lower magnitude** than what was forecasted in earlier UN reports, such as the 2022 revision.
 
• The primary reason for this downward revision is the faster-than-anticipated decline in **fertility rates** in several large and populous nations, coupled with increasing mortality rates in specific regions due to health crises or socio-economic factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Current Demographic Status**:

 
 
• As of **2024**, the world population is estimated to have reached **8.2 billion**.
 
• In **2024**, the global **fertility rate** stands at approximately **2.25 births per woman**, which is just above the replacement level of **2.1** required for long-term population stability.
 
• More than **60 countries** have already reached their population peak or are expected to do so before **2054**, including nations like **China**, **Germany**, **Japan**, and the **Russian Federation**.
 
 
 
• **Life Expectancy and Aging**:
 
 
• Global **life expectancy** at birth reached **73.3 years** in **2024** and is projected to rise to **77.4 years** by **2054**.
 
• By the late **2070s**, the number of persons aged **65 or older** is projected to exceed the number of children under age **18**, indicating a significant global demographic shift toward an aging population.
 
• The report highlights that by **2054**, nearly **one in five** people globally will be aged **65 or older**.

questions.question: Which of the following rulers of the Maitraka dynasty attended Harshavardhana’s assembly at Prayaga?

questions.question: Which of the following goddesses is primarily worshipped during the Gangaur festival of Rajasthan?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

• The term **Gangaur** is derived from two words: **Gan**, which represents **Lord Shiva**, and **Gaur** (or Gauri), which represents **Goddess Parvati**. The festival celebrates the divine union and marital fidelity of this celestial couple.
 
• It is one of the most important and vivid festivals in **Rajasthan**, observed with great fervor by women. Married women worship the goddess for the **longevity and health** of their husbands, while unmarried girls pray to find a suitable and virtuous life partner.
 
• The festivities begin on the day following **Holi** and continue for **18 days**, reaching their peak on the third day of the **Shukla Paksha** in the Hindu month of **Chaitra**.
 
• Rituals involve the creation of clay or wooden idols of **Isar** (Shiva) and **Gauri** (Parvati). These images are beautifully dressed in traditional attire, adorned with jewelry, and worshipped with **henna** (Mehendi), flowers, and special sweets like **Ghewar**.
 
• The festival concludes with a grand **visarjan** (immersion) ceremony, where the idols are carried in a colorful procession to a local **Johad** (pond), lake, or well, symbolizing **Gauri** returning to her husband's home.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regional Variations and Significance**:

• **Udaipur**: A distinct boat procession is organized on **Lake Pichola**, where the idols are placed on decorated boats starting from the **Gangaur Ghat**.
 
• **Goddess Saraswati**: She is the deity of **knowledge, wisdom, and arts**. Her primary festival is **Vasant Panchami**, where devotees wear yellow garments and offer prayers for academic success.
 
• **Goddess Durga**: Representing **Shakti** or divine feminine power, she is the central figure of **Navratri** and **Durga Puja**, symbolizing the victory of good over evil.
 
• **Goddess Lakshmi**: The goddess of **wealth, fortune, and prosperity**, she is primarily worshipped during **Diwali** and **Lakshmi Puja** across India.

questions.question: Which type of soil is most suitable for cotton cultivation in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Black Soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Black Soil**, also known as **Regur Soil** or **Black Cotton Soil**, is considered the most suitable for cotton cultivation due to its unique physical and chemical properties.
 
• It is predominantly found in the **Deccan Trap** region (basaltic area) across states like **Maharashtra**, **Gujarat**, **Madhya Pradesh**, and parts of **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• The soil is composed of extremely fine **clayey material**, which gives it a remarkable capacity to **retain moisture** for long durations, supporting the plant during dry spells.
 
• During the dry season, the soil develops deep **cracks**, allowing for proper **aeration** and the diffusion of oxygen deep into the layers, a process often described as **self-plowing**.
 
• This soil is rich in essential plant nutrients such as **Calcium Carbonate**, **Magnesium**, **Potash**, and **Lime**, although it is generally poor in phosphorus content.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alluvial Soil**:

 
 
• Formed by the deposition of silt by the **Indus**, **Ganga**, and **Brahmaputra** river systems.
 
• It is highly fertile and supports crops like **Rice**, **Wheat**, and **Sugarcane**.
 
 
 
• **Red Soil**:

questions.question: Which term refers to the quantitative study of reactants and products in a chemical reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stoichiometry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stoichiometry** is the section of chemistry that involves the **quantitative calculation** of the masses and volumes of reactants and products participating in a chemical reaction.
 
• The concept is fundamentally based on the **Law of Conservation of Mass**, which necessitates that the total mass of reactants must equal the total mass of products, as atoms are only rearranged during a reaction.
 
• The term is etymologically derived from the Greek words **'stoicheion'**, meaning element, and **'metron'**, meaning measure, effectively signifying the measurement of chemical elements.
 
• It utilizes **balanced chemical equations** and **stoichiometric coefficients** to establish molar ratios, which serve as conversion factors to determine the theoretical yield of a chemical process.
 
• These calculations are essential in industrial chemistry for optimizing **feedstock amounts** and predicting the efficiency of large-scale chemical syntheses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mole fraction**:

 
 
• Defined as the ratio of the **number of moles** of a particular component to the total number of moles of all substances present in a solution or mixture.
 
• It is a **dimensionless quantity** and is independent of temperature changes.
 
 
 
• **Mass per cent**:
 
 
• A concentration expression representing the **mass of a solute** divided by the total mass of the solution, multiplied by 100.
 
• It is commonly used in commercial chemical labeling to denote the **purity** or concentration of reagents.
 
 
 
• **Molarity**:
 
 
• Determined by the **number of moles** of solute dissolved in exactly one liter of solution (moles per liter).
 
• Unlike molality, molarity is **temperature-dependent** because the volume of a liquid expands or contracts with temperature fluctuations.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the gaseous state of matter?

options.text: Definite volume but no definite shape
Negligible intermolecular forces and high compressibility
Strong intermolecular forces and fixed shape

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Negligible intermolecular forces and high compressibility**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Matter in the **gaseous state** consists of particles that are far apart from each other, resulting in **maximum intermolecular spaces** compared to solids and liquids.
 
• Due to these large distances, the **intermolecular forces of attraction** between gas particles are **negligible**, allowing them to move freely and randomly in all directions at high velocities.
 
• The presence of vast empty spaces between molecules allows gases to be easily squeezed into smaller volumes when pressure is applied, leading to **high compressibility**.
 
• Gases lack a **definite shape** and a **definite volume**; they expand to completely fill whatever container they are placed in, exerting **uniform pressure** on the container walls.
 
• The **kinetic energy** of gas molecules is significantly higher than that of molecules in the solid or liquid states, which contributes to their rapid **diffusion** and lack of structural rigidity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solid State**:

 
 
• Characterized by **strong intermolecular forces** that keep particles in fixed positions.
 
• Possesses **high rigidity**, a **fixed shape**, and a **definite volume**.
 
• The **compressibility** is negligible because particles are already closely packed.
 
 
 
• **Liquid State**:
 
 
• Particles have **intermediate intermolecular forces**, allowing them to slide past one another.
 
• Maintains a **definite volume** but takes the **shape of the container** (no fixed shape).
 
• Liquids are generally considered **incompressible** for most practical purposes, though slightly more compressible than solids.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Density**:
 
 
• Gases generally have the **lowest density** among the three primary states of matter because their mass is spread over a much larger volume.
 
• This property, combined with high mobility, makes them essential in applications like **LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas)** and **CNG (Compressed Natural Gas)** storage.

questions.question: What is the purpose of using different file types with extensions in an operating system like MS Windows?

options.text: To hide file content and remove the content from file
To allow the OS to determine which application should open the file
To increase file size and make changes in file
To make file names longer and rename file

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To allow the OS to determine which application should open the file**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **file extension** is a suffix consisting of a period followed by a few characters (e.g., **.exe**, **.pdf**, **.txt**) that is appended to the end of a filename in an **Operating System** like **Microsoft Windows**.
 
• The primary function of these extensions is to assist the **OS** in identifying the **file format** and the internal structure of the data stored within the file.
 
• Windows utilizes a mechanism called **File Association** to link specific extensions with their corresponding **default applications**; this ensures that when a user double-clicks a file, the correct software is launched automatically.
 
• The **Windows Registry** (specifically the **HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT** hive) acts as a database that maps these extensions to specific **executable programs**, facilitating seamless **human-computer interaction**.
 
• By identifying the file type, the system can determine which **icon** to display and which specific actions (like **Open**, **Edit**, or **Print**) are available in the **Context Menu** for that particular file.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evolution of File Extensions**:

 
 
• The concept of extensions stems from the **MS-DOS** era, which followed the **8.3 filename** convention (a name up to 8 characters and an extension up to 3 characters).
 
• While modern **NTFS** and **exFAT** file systems support much longer filenames, the extension remains the standard method for **metadata** identification in Windows.
 
 
 
• **Common Extension Categories**:
 
 
• **Productivity**: **.xlsx** (Excel), **.pptx** (PowerPoint), and **.docx** (Word) allow the OS to route documents to the **Microsoft Office Suite**.
 
• **System & Execution**: **.dll** (Dynamic Link Library) and **.sys** (System files) indicate files that are used by the system itself rather than user-facing applications.
 
• **Media**: Extensions like **.mp3** (audio) and **.mp4** (video) trigger **media players** or **codecs** for decompression and playback.
 
 
 
• **User Control**:
 
 
• Users can manually change associations via the **Control Panel** or **Settings** app, allowing them to choose a preferred browser for **.html** files or a specific editor for **.py** scripts.
 
• Although users can rename extensions, doing so does not convert the file's **encoding**; for example, renaming a **.txt** to **.jpg** will make the OS attempt to open it with an **Image Viewer**, which will fail to render the text data.

questions.question: Which of the following provisions requires ratification by the legislatures of NOT less than half the States for amendment under Article 368(2), making it a 'rigid' feature?

__
 
• **Article 368** of the **Indian Constitution** provides the procedure for constitutional amendments. While most amendments require a **Special Majority** (two-thirds of members present and voting and a majority of total membership), certain **federal features** require a more rigid process involving **ratification** by the legislatures of at least **half of the States**.
 
• The **Manner of election of the President of India**, covered under **Articles 54 and 55**, is explicitly listed under the proviso to **Article 368(2)**. This is because the **President** is elected by an **Electoral College** that includes elected members of **State Legislative Assemblies**, making it a critical **federal provision**.
 
• The requirement for **State Ratification** ensures that the **Union Parliament** cannot unilaterally alter the **federal structure** or the balance of power between the center and the states. Other provisions requiring this include the **Seventh Schedule**, the **Supreme Court and High Courts**, and **Article 368** itself.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Rigid Provisions**:

 
 
• **Extent of executive power** of the Union and the States (**Articles 73 and 162**).
 
• **Representation of States in Parliament** (provisions in the **Fourth Schedule**).
 
• Any change to the **Lists** in the **Seventh Schedule** (Union, State, and Concurrent Lists).
 
 
 
• **Citizenship acquisition and termination**:
 
 
• Provisions regarding **Citizenship** are governed by **Part II** of the Constitution and the **Citizenship Act, 1955**. Under **Article 11**, **Parliament** has the power to regulate citizenship by **Simple Majority**; thus, it does not require the rigid procedure of **Article 368(2)**.
 
 
 
• **Duration of Lok Sabha**:
 
 
• The term of the **House of the People** is generally governed by **Article 83**. While changing the fundamental structure might require a **Special Majority**, it is not explicitly listed as a federal provision requiring **State Ratification** unless it interferes with the representation of states.

questions.question: In Windows, which file extension represents a dynamic-link library containing reusable code shared across applications?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dynamic Link Library (DLL)** is a Microsoft implementation of the shared library concept in the **Windows Operating System**. It contains code and data that can be used by more than one program at the same time.
 
• Unlike an executable (**.exe**), a DLL cannot be run directly; it must be called by other code that is already executing. These files allow for **modular programming**, where developers can separate different components of a software into unique modules.
 
• The primary advantage of **.dll** files is **memory efficiency**. Because multiple applications can share a single copy of a DLL loaded into the **RAM**, the system avoids loading duplicate code for common tasks like printing or file management.
 
• DLLs facilitate **dynamic linking**, which means the link between an application and the library is established at **runtime** rather than when the application is compiled. This reduces the size of the application **executable** files.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **.drv (Device Driver):**

 
 
• These files are specialized libraries used by the **Operating System** to communicate with hardware devices.
 
• They contain instructions that tell the OS how to interact with components like **graphics cards**, printers, or sound cards.
 
 
 
• **.tmp (Temporary File):**
 
 
• These are generated by applications or the OS to store information temporarily while a **process** is running or a new file is being created.
 
• They are usually deleted automatically once the task is finished or the program is closed to free up **storage space**.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of DLL Files:**
 
 
• **Easier Maintenance:** When a function within a DLL needs an update or a bug fix, only the DLL needs to be replaced, rather than reinstalling the entire software suite.
 
• **Resource Sharing:** DLLs allow for the sharing of resources like **icons**, strings, and **dialog boxes** across various Windows applications.
 
• **Language Independence:** A DLL written in **C++** can be utilized by applications written in other languages like **Visual Basic** or **C#**.

questions.question: Action and reaction forces are exerted on which bodies during an interaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Two different bodies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Newton's Third Law of Motion**, for every action, there is always an **equal and opposite reaction**.
 
• Action and reaction forces represent the **mutual interaction** between two objects; they never occur in isolation but always in **pairs**.
 
• The fundamental property of these forces is that the **action force** is exerted by the first body on the second, while the **reaction force** is exerted by the second body back on the first. Therefore, they act on **two different bodies**.
 
• Because these forces act on **distinct objects**, they do not result in a **net force of zero** on a single body. This is why a person can walk: the foot pushes the ground backward (action on ground), and the ground pushes the foot forward (reaction on person).
 
• These forces are **simultaneous**, meaning there is no time lag between the application of the action and the occurrence of the reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Properties of Action-Reaction Pairs:
 
 
• **Direction**: The forces act along the same line but in **exactly opposite directions**.
 
• **Magnitude**: The **numerical value** of the force exerted by object A on B is identical to the force exerted by object B on A.
 
• **Nature of Force**: Both forces are of the **same physical nature**; for instance, if the action is a **magnetic force**, the reaction must also be a magnetic force.
 
 
 
• Clarification of Incorrect Concepts:
 
 
• **The same body**: If action and reaction forces acted on the same body, they would cancel each other out, and the body would remain in its **state of rest or uniform motion** regardless of the force applied.
 
• **State of Motion**: These forces apply to all interactions regardless of whether the bodies are **at rest** or **moving**. The law is a universal principle of **classical mechanics**.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.
(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(2, 5, 7)
(3, 10, 13)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic:**

**1) Second number = (First number)² + 1**

**2) Third number = First number + Second number**

For the first set **(2, 5, 7)**:

⇒ (2)² + 1 = 4 + 1 = 5 (**Second number**)

⇒ 2 + 5 = 7 (**Third number**)

For the second set **(3, 10, 13)**:

⇒ (3)² + 1 = 9 + 1 = 10 (**Second number**)

⇒ 3 + 10 = 13 (**Third number**)

Applying the same logic to the set **(6, 37, 43)**:

⇒ (6)² + 1 = 36 + 1 = 37 (**Second number**)

⇒ 6 + 37 = 43 (**Third number**)

Hence, the correct answer is **'Option 2'**.
